doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The Blue Three, Wellstood's death and his succession of trios
summary: Davern recalls the Blue Three with Bobby Rosengarden and Dick Wellstood in 1981 and his other trios and the Breezin' Along group.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Ah, the Hot Three. No the Blue Three.
Bobby Rosengarden, Dick Wellstood and yours truly, 1981.
I once asked Joe Venuti what happened, how he felt after Eddie Lang died. And he said it was like half of me died. Well when Wellstood died I felt that way.
That’s something to sustain a band like that too without a bass player I think.

Oh we were brilliant. We really enjoyed. I made a conscious effort to play trios. So I did a trio with Art Hodes and Don DeMicheal, and then they died. And then it was Ralph Sutton and Gus Johnson and Gus Johnson died. Then I did one with Dick Wellstood and Bobby Rosengarden, and Dick died. And then, you know, but after a while, so like I switched to guitars. And they’re all alive. In fact we’re going to do it tonight, the Breezin’ Along group. I’ll have fun with that. Because Howard Alden can read my mind, Bucky plays nonparalleled rhythm, nobody plays better than him.
